description: deixis-core construction-rejection vectors — the duplicate-key refusal of docs/TREE.md. Hand-authored from the spec, not generated by an implementation. Each case is a node spelling whose construction must fail with the stable rejection code `duplicate_key`, reporting the duplicated key's exact bytes (`key`, hex). deixis has no policy for which duplicate would win, so it declines to choose — rejection is unconditional, and equal children do not soften it. Every judgment is append-only except an explicit erratum.

cases.name: duplicate-key-adjacent
cases.note: The plain case: the same key twice, back to back.

cases.name: duplicate-key-nonadjacent
cases.note: The duplicates are separated in insertion order; an implementation checking only adjacent input pairs misses this.

cases.name: duplicate-empty-key
cases.note: The empty key duplicates like any other key.

cases.name: duplicate-multibyte-key
cases.note: Whole-key octet equality decides duplication; length is part of the key.

cases.name: duplicate-with-equal-children
cases.note: Rejection is about the domain, not the children — identical children are still a duplicate key.

cases.name: duplicate-in-nested-struct
cases.note: The offense sits one level down; a sound outer construction does not launder an inner duplicate.
